general_information.Description: This course aims to provide students in the Digital Automotive Engineering program with a comprehensive understanding and hands-on competencies in the AUTOSAR Classic platform. The course centers on three fundamental pillars of modern automotive software: layered software architecture, real-time operating systems (RTOS), and diagnostic systems. Through this course, students will: - Understand layered AUTOSAR architecture: Learn the roles of the Application (ASW), Runtime Environment (RTE), and Basic Software (BSW), and design hardware-independent Software Components (SWC) based on the Virtual Function Bus (VFB) concept. - Gain practical experience with AUTOSAR OS (RTOS): Configure and manage multitasking systems, including task creation, priority assignment, scheduling mechanisms, and timing control using Alarms and Schedule Tables. - Apply basic diagnostic mechanisms: Explore international diagnostic standards (ISO 14229 – UDS) and understand the roles of DCM, DEM, and NvM modules in automotive software systems. - Develop a practical AUTOSAR project: Use the MaaZ Edu SDK and SCons build environment to design ARXML configurations, generate RTE code, and deploy application logic on simulated or hardware platforms. By the end of the course, students will possess both theoretical knowledge of AUTOSAR and practical skills in real-time system performance—an essential competency for ECU software engineers in the automotive industry.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information
general_information.Tools: 1. Design tools: ARXML editing tools for SWC/VFB definition and CanDB++ for CAN network design. 2. Programming: Use an IDE (e.g., VS Code) to implement application logic in Runnables. 3. Real-time control: (FreeRTOS + Wrapper) or AUTOSAR OS for configuring Tasks and the Scheduler. 4. Compilation: SCons build system. 5. Diagnostics: MaaZ Edu SDK providing DCM, DEM, and NvM libraries for API-based integration. 5. Hardware: MaaZ Devkit

description: This course aims to provide students in the Digital Automotive Engineering program with a comprehensive understanding and hands-on competencies in the AUTOSAR Classic platform. The course centers on three fundamental pillars of modern automotive software: layered software architecture, real-time operating systems (RTOS), and diagnostic systems. Through this course, students will: - Understand layered AUTOSAR architecture: Learn the roles of the Application (ASW), Runtime Environment (RTE), and Basic Software (BSW), and design hardware-independent Software Components (SWC) based on the Virtual Function Bus (VFB) concept. - Gain practical experience with AUTOSAR OS (RTOS): Configure and manage multitasking systems, including task creation, priority assignment, scheduling mechanisms, and timing control using Alarms and Schedule Tables. - Apply basic diagnostic mechanisms: Explore international diagnostic standards (ISO 14229 – UDS) and understand the roles of DCM, DEM, and NvM modules in automotive software systems. - Develop a practical AUTOSAR project: Use the MaaZ Edu SDK and SCons build environment to design ARXML configurations, generate RTE code, and deploy application logic on simulated or hardware platforms. By the end of the course, students will possess both theoretical knowledge of AUTOSAR and practical skills in real-time system performance—an essential competency for ECU software engineers in the automotive industry.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Analyze and design Software Component (SWC) architecture, Ports, and Interfaces based on the AUTOSAR methodology to construct the Virtual Functional Bus (VFB) communication diagram.
Configure and operate the AUTOSAR real-time operating system (AUTOSAR OS), including task management (multitasking), scheduling, and periodic execution control using Schedule Tables and Alarms.
Use and integrate basic diagnostic services (UDS Services) through the DCM and DEM modules to monitor system status.
Implement and validate the storage of diagnostic and user data in non-volatile memory (NvM) through the AUTOSAR memory abstraction layer.
Design, implement, and complete an automotive software project (Final Project) on the MaaZ Edu platform integrating real-time logic processing and diagnostic management.
Present and document the system through technical reports, including ARXML configuration, Task diagrams, and execution results on hardware or simulation platforms.

schedule.Topic: Course Introduction & Environment Setup: Course structure; installation of the MaaZ Edu SDK; configuration of environment variables and the SCons build system.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Tool installation and environment setup: Configure environment variables for SCons and verify the compiler connection.

schedule.Topic: AUTOSAR Architecture Overview: Analysis of the three main layers: Application (ASW), Runtime Environment (RTE), and Basic Software (BSW).
schedule.Student's Tasks: Read the documentation, redraw the layered architecture diagram, and identify the position of the SWC.

schedule.Topic: Methodology & ARXML Templates: Study the development process from system design to ECU code generation.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Analyze the structure of a sample ARXML file and study the basic XML tags used within it.

schedule.Topic: Software Components (SWC) Design: Define different types of SWCs (Atomic, Composition, and Sensor–Actuator).
schedule.Student's Tasks: Classify automotive features into the corresponding SWC types.

schedule.Topic: Sender–Receiver Interface (S/R): 1-to-n and n-to-1 data communication mechanisms; concept of Data Elements.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Design data communication interfaces (e.g., vehicle speed, button status).

schedule.Topic: Client–Server Interface (C/S): Request–response function call mechanism; definition of Operations and Arguments.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Design service request interfaces (e.g., reading/writing NvM memory).

schedule.Topic: Ports & Port Interfaces: Define P-Ports (Provide) and R-Ports (Require).
schedule.Student's Tasks: Map interfaces to specific ports on a Software Component.

schedule.Topic: Virtual Function Bus (VFB) Theory: Virtual communication mechanism and hardware independence of the application layer.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Draw a virtual connection diagram between SWCs without considering ECU mapping.

schedule.Topic: Lab 1 (Part1) – Modeling with ARXML Editor: Practice creating a project and designing SWCs using the tool.
schedule.Student Materials: Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, Lab guide file.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Tool: ARXML Editor. Create two SWCs: Ignition_SWC and Engine_Control_SWC.

schedule.Topic: Lab 1 (Par2) – VFB Connection: Practice connecting communication ports and validating the configuration.
schedule.Student Materials: Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, Lab guide file.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Tool: ARXML Editor. Connect the Ports and run the validation check in the tool.

schedule.Topic: RTE Fundamentals & Internal Behavior: Triggering events and executable functions (Runnables).
schedule.Student's Tasks: Identify Timing Events (e.g., execution every 10 ms) for Runnables.

schedule.Topic: RTE Code Generation: Use tools to automatically generate the middleware source code.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Tool: RTE Generator. Execute code generation; analyze the Rte.c file and understand the APIs Rte_Read and Rte_Write.

schedule.Topic: Assignment 1 (Part1) – System Architecture: Design an automatic lighting control system with three SWCs.
schedule.Student Materials: Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, Assignment guide file.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Tool: ARXML Editor. Design the complete set of interfaces for the system, including the Sensor, Logic, and Actuator components.

schedule.Topic: Assignment 1 (Part2) – Integration & Build: Implement C logic for the Runnables and build the project.
schedule.Student Materials: Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, Assignment guide file.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Tool: SCons. Complete the application logic, run the SCons build script, and execute the project on the simulator.

schedule.Topic: Assignment 1 Review & Demo: Present and evaluate the Milestone 1 project deliverables.
schedule.Student Materials: Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, Assignment guide file.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Present the VFB diagram, demonstrate the application logic running on the simulator, and submit the report.

schedule.Topic: RTOS Concepts in Automotive: How FreeRTOS simulates AUTOSAR BCC/ECC standards and the concept of time units (tick rate).
schedule.Student's Tasks: Initialize a base project with FreeRTOS and configure "configTICK_RATE_HZ" to achieve 1 ms timing resolution.

schedule.Topic: RTOS Concepts in Automotive: How FreeRTOS simulates AUTOSAR BCC/ECC standards and the concept of time units (tick rate). Cont.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Initialize a base project with FreeRTOS and configure "configTICK_RATE_HZ" to achieve 1 ms timing resolution.

schedule.Topic: Task Configuration (Static vs. Dynamic): Define task priority and stack size for each application task.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Declare the task list in the configuration file and assign priority levels to Runnable functions.

schedule.Topic: Task Configuration (Static vs. Dynamic): Define task priority and stack size for each application task. Cont.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Declare the task list in the configuration file and assign priority levels to Runnable functions.

schedule.Topic: Scheduling Policy (Preemptive): Preemption mechanism and how the scheduler selects the next ready task for execution.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Simulate a scenario with two tasks of the same priority and observe the Round-robin scheduling mechanism.

schedule.Topic: Scheduling Policy (Preemptive): Preemption mechanism and how the scheduler selects the next ready task for execution. Cont.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Simulate a scenario with two tasks of the same priority and observe the Round-robin scheduling mechanism.

schedule.Topic: Synchronization with Events: Use Event Groups to synchronize Runnables (corresponding to AUTOSAR Events).
schedule.Student's Tasks: Implement logic where Task B waits for an Event bit from Task A before starting data processing.

schedule.Topic: Synchronization with Events: Use Event Groups to synchronize Runnables (corresponding to AUTOSAR Events). Cont.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Implement logic where Task B waits for an Event bit from Task A before starting data processing.

schedule.Topic: Software Timers & Alarms: Simulate AUTOSAR Alarms using FreeRTOS software timers to trigger periodic task execution.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Configure timers to automatically set events or resume tasks every 10 ms, 50 ms, and 100 ms.

schedule.Topic: Software Timers & Alarms: Simulate AUTOSAR Alarms using FreeRTOS software timers to trigger periodic task execution. Cont.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Configure timers to automatically set events or resume tasks every 10 ms, 50 ms, and 100 ms.

schedule.Topic: Schedule Table Simulation: Slot-based execution scheduling techniques to avoid CPU conflicts.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Design a timing schedule: Task_A starts at tick 0, Task_B at tick 5, and Task_C at tick 10.

schedule.Topic: Schedule Table Simulation: Slot-based execution scheduling techniques to avoid CPU conflicts. Cont.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Design a timing schedule: Task_A starts at tick 0, Task_B at tick 5, and Task_C at tick 10.

schedule.Topic: Lab 2 (Part1) – OS Configuration Tool: Use the wrapper to configure tasks without writing initialization code.
schedule.Student Materials: Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, Lab guide file.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Tool: SCons + configuration header. Define task parameters in the header file according to the wrapper standard.

schedule.Topic: Lab 2 (Part2) – Multitasking Debug: Verify the task execution order and actual timing behavior.
schedule.Student Materials: Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, Lab guide file.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Tool: Terminal/Simulator. Print real-time logs to measure the jitter of 10 ms tasks.

schedule.Topic: Resource Management (Mutex/Semaphore): Protect shared data (global variables) between tasks.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Practice using a mutex to protect the VehicleSpeed variable when accessed by multiple tasks.

schedule.Topic: Resource Management (Mutex/Semaphore): Protect shared data (global variables) between tasks. Cont.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Practice using a mutex to protect the VehicleSpeed variable when accessed by multiple tasks.

schedule.Topic: RTE & OS Integration: Map the Runnables from Part 1 to the newly created periodic Tasks.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Invoke the Rte_Runnable_... functions within the loop of the corresponding RTOS task.

schedule.Topic: Assignment 2 (Part1) – RTOS Architecture Design: Plan the execution architecture for the ECU.
schedule.Student Materials: Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, Assignment guide file.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Design a priority matrix and a timing table for five different application tasks.

schedule.Topic: Assignment 2 (Part2) – Build System with SCons: Manage the build process for a multitasking project.
schedule.Student Materials: Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, Assignment guide file.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Tool: SCons. Write build scripts to manage the source files of the OS, wrapper, and application.

schedule.Topic: Assignment 2 (Part3) – Optimization & Performance: Optimize the system for the smoothest performance.
schedule.Student Materials: Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, Assignment guide file.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Adjust task priorities and execution periods to achieve optimal CPU usage (below 60%).

schedule.Topic: Assignment 2 Review: System demonstration and presentation.
schedule.Student Materials: Slide, Reference manual, Course syllabus, Assignment guide file.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Demo: Run the system on the simulator and demonstrate system stability and accurate timing.

schedule.Topic: Diagnostic Overview: Role of diagnostics in the vehicle lifecycle; introduction to the ISO 14229 (UDS) standard; concept of Tester vs. ECU.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Read documentation on diagnostic protocol layers and analyze the purposes of reading fault codes (DTCs) and data identifiers (DIDs).

schedule.Topic: Diagnostic Overview: Role of diagnostics in the vehicle lifecycle; introduction to the ISO 14229 (UDS) standard; concept of Tester vs. ECU. Cont.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Read documentation on diagnostic protocol layers and analyze the purposes of reading fault codes (DTCs) and data identifiers (DIDs).

schedule.Topic: Unified Diagnostic Services (UDS): Detailed overview of services: 0x10 (Session Control), 0x22 (ReadDataByID), 0x2E (WriteDataByID), and 0x11 (ECU Reset).
schedule.Student's Tasks: Practice analyzing the structure of Request/Response messages and distinguish between Positive and Negative Responses.

schedule.Topic: Unified Diagnostic Services (UDS): Detailed overview of services: 0x10 (Session Control), 0x22 (ReadDataByID), 0x2E (WriteDataByID), and 0x11 (ECU Reset). Cont.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Practice analyzing the structure of Request/Response messages and distinguish between Positive and Negative Responses.

schedule.Topic: Diagnostic Communication Manager (DCM): Structure of the DCM module in AUTOSAR, including the DSL (Link), DSD (Delivery), and DSP (Processing) layers.
schedule.Student's Tasks: Study how the DCM routes messages from the tester to the application layer.

schedule.Topic: Diagnostic Communication Manager (DCM): Structure of the DCM module in AUTOSAR, including the DSL (Link), DSD (Delivery), and DSP (Processing) layers. Cont.

schedule.Topic: DEM (Diagnostic Event Manager): System fault management; definition of Events and Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs); structure of the DTC Status Byte.

schedule.Topic: NvM (Non-Volatile Memory): Management of non-volatile memory; concepts of RAM blocks and NV blocks; data synchronization mechanisms.
